notes:
ATTEMPT 3 of 3. The shoulder CONSTRUCTION is right — soft, unpadded, no built-up corner — but it is framed out of its own photograph at both ends, which is a major placement fault for this particular option and not a cosmetic one.

WORTH RECORDING UPSTREAM, because this is the third attempt to lose to the same cause: THE PROMPT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT FRAMING. The composition template opens every prompt with 'the subject filling 40-80% of the frame' and 'Frame on the shoulder and sleeve head; the detail must read clearly and sharply' — close-crop language. The FRAMING LOCK then says 'THIS IS A WIDE SHOT, NOT A CLOSE CROP. THIS PARAGRAPH OUTRANKS THE CLOSE-CROP MANDATE... MOVE THE CAMERA BACK.' Declaring one paragraph the winner does not make the model drop the other; across three attempts the close-crop language has won every time.

The general lesson, which applies to every option whose subject is a RELATIONSHIP across the garment rather than a single detail — both shoulders, both lapels, a left/right pocket difference, a symmetric pair — is that the 40-80% dominance default is wrong for them and cannot be overridden by adding a louder paragraph. It has to not be emitted in the first place. That is a change to camera.mjs, not to a correction clause, and it is beyond what a retry can fix.

Recording UNMET honestly rather than waiving. A waiver requires zero critical/major findings and this has a major, so it does not qualify — and it should not: the option is not adequately shown.
